title: The batch judge's dry-run constants are set from the measured Haiku 5.5 output per item
goal: factdiff.JUDGE_REPLY_TOKENS and JUDGE_CALL_TOKENS are set from the measured Haiku 5.5 output per item (thinking tokens count as output, the logs census's dry run was 4.7 times low), so the dry run and the call cap track the real spend.

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'_tools'); import factdiff as f; sys.exit(0 if 333 <= f.JUDGE_REPLY_TOKENS <= 555 and 6000 <= f.JUDGE_CALL_TOKENS <= 12000 else 1)

notes: Premise: factdiff.JUDGE_REPLY_TOKENS is 80 and JUDGE_CALL_TOKENS 4000, which priced the logs census's judge dry run at 3,600 out and 18,134 in; the run read 19,592 out and 44,436 in over 4 calls (kb/_self/reports/fact-diff.md:297, 'Estimate against run'). Premise run 2026-10-12: import factdiff prints 80 4000; reproduces. Figures the check bounds (+-25%): output 19,592 over the 45 dry-run items is about 435 per item (range 333 to 555); input 44,436 less about 8,200 of passages over 4 calls is about 9,000 per call (range 6,000 to 12,000). The worker measures its own figure from that report and a judge ops row where one exists; census.py reads both constants (dry run, line 1699). Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 8 of 19, "Census and fact diff: anchor runs write only their own rows, judge confirms are sampled, cost figures are measured"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed.
